subject: Discovery recap: data governance and logging constraints for Clearwave
content:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@clearwave.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Discovery recap: data governance and logging constraints for Clearwave

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have everything in one place.

Key pain points you shared
- Customer support search accuracy is declining when using current embeddings pipeline; you suspect data leakage from transient logs.
- Stringent audit and evidence requirements for transactions and user-identifiable events — need immutable audit trails for 12+ months for certain transaction types.
- Field-level PII (names, emails, SSNs) must never be written to persistent inference logs in cleartext.
- Need the ability to selectively redact sensitive fields before any logs are stored or exported.

Current stack summary (from our call)
- Inference: hosted microservice in GCP us-central for latency-sensitive features.
- Logging: mix of structured telemetry (BigQuery) and plain-text application logs forwarded to third-party SIEM.
- Auth: SAML SSO + key rotation via internal KMS.

Success criteria you outlined
1) Proof that inference requests do not retain raw PII in persisted logs (either via redaction or tokenization).
2) Ability to retain audit logs for required windows (12 months for transaction audit, 90 days for inference request metadata) with tamper-evidence.
3) Demonstrable access controls + role-separated audit for log downloads (SOC2-aligned).
4) Latency target: p95 < 200ms for short text queries (under 512 tokens) in EU region.
5) Clear escalation path and SLAs for incident response.

Items we will deliver
- A short tech note showing how Redwood handles request/response logging, options for prefix/KV caching, and the redaction pipeline (PDF attached: redwood-discovery-notes-20261124.pdf).
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted) and our DPA template — will share in the next 48–72 hours.
- Proposed mutual action plan (attached Excel with milestones: initial pilot, security review, production rollout).

Questions / clarifications from today
- You mentioned transaction-level retention of ~12 months for a subset of events; can you confirm which event types need full retention vs. those that can adhere to a 90-day window?
- Do you require on-premises deployment options for the pilot or would a VPC-private deployment in an EU cloud region be sufficient?

Next steps
1) I’ll send the SOC2 report, our DPA draft, and an anonymized log sample by EOD Thursday.
2) Markus to schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk through the redaction options and demo log sanitization.
3) If helpful, Marissa will prepare a short architecture diagram showing where Redwood stores telemetry vs. audit logs.

Proposed meeting times for the technical deep-dive (all times CET): Wed 11/25 10:00–11:00, Thu 11/26 15:00–16:00. Let me know what works and we’ll lock it.

Best,

Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

--- Attachment stubs: redwood-discovery-notes-20261124.pdf (3 pages), initial-MAP-CLW-20261124.xlsx (MAP worksheet)

------------------------------------------------------------
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@clearwave.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearwave Security Team <security@clearwave.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data governance and logging constraints for Clearwave

Monica —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side after reviewing internally:
- Event classification: "transaction" events (payments/refunds) need 13 months retention per our finance policy; session-level inference metadata (embedding IDs, anonymized latencies) can be 90 days. We need a way to tag events so retention policies can be automated.
- Redaction: field-level redaction is a must. We also want an option for token-level hashing before logs are persisted (for identifiers like account numbers). Can Redwood support pluggable redaction hooks or do we need to pre-process upstream?
- Data residency: pilot must run in an EU region and all backups/audit exports must stay in EU.
- Evidence: for procurement we’ll need a sample immutable audit export and a description of tamper-evidence controls.

Attached is our data-classification spreadsheet; it includes which event types are "transactional" vs "support".

We can do the technical deep-dive Thu 11/26 15:00 CET (that works for Mark and me). Please include Markus and your security lead.

Elena
Head of Engineering Operations | Clearwave Financial
elena.morris@clearwave.com | +44 20 7946 0123

--- Attachment stub: clearwave-data-classification.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@clearwave.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data governance and logging constraints for Clearwave

Thanks, Elena — great notes and the spreadsheet is helpful. Confirming we’ll do Thu 11/26 15:00 CET for the technical deep-dive (we’ll send a calendar invite shortly).

Immediate commitments from our side
- Deliverables by EOD Thursday: SOC2 summary + redacted Type II, DPA draft, anonymized log sample with example redaction patterns. (Owner: Monica)
- Technical deep-dive to include a demonstration of: 1) pre-ingest field-level redaction, 2) token-hashing option, 3) retention policy tagging and automated export. (Owner: Markus)
- Architecture diagram showing separation of transit telemetry vs. persistent audit store and EU-region deployment options. (Owner: Marissa)

Notes for the deep-dive: Markus will demo both hosted EU deployment and our private (customer-managed) control plane options — he’ll show how redaction hooks can run in an ingestion lane so PII never persists in long-term storage.

Logistics: Elena, we noted the 13-month requirement for "transaction" events; Markus will propose an event-tagging approach during the demo so policy enforcement can be automated.

If you need a non-disclosure in place before we share some of the artifacts, please flag and we’ll get our legal team on it.

Thanks — looking forward to the next meeting.

Monica
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
